text:
arjun: quick one — hitting `Unauthorized` on `unwrapKey` when our private instance talks to a customer AKV. flow: GH Actions federated creds -> app reg in customer's tenant -> token -> call AKV to unwrap envelope key. anyone done this exact wiring cross-tenant?

marta: we ran into similar last quarter. short answer: the token needs a principal that actually exists in the vault's tenant and has RBAC or access-policy perms on the vault. federated cred by itself is just a way to mint tokens for an app principal, but that principal must be known to the tenant where the vault lives.

kevin: +1. prefer RBAC over access policies for this (less manual mapping). make sure the principal has the built-in role `Key Vault Crypto User` (or equivalent) on the vault scope. required key ops: `wrapKey`, `unwrapKey`, `get`. example role assign:
```
az role assignment create \\n  --assignee-object-id <APP_OBJECT_ID> \\n  --role "Key Vault Crypto User" \\n  --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>
```

arjun: here's the snippet from the app logs: `Azure.RequestFailedException: Status: 401 (Unauthorized) ErrorCode: AuthenticationFailed Message: Access denied to key unwrap.` we created an app registration in our infra tenant and added a federated credential in GH. But the customer's vault is in a different tenant — maybe the SP object id is not present there.

deploy-bot: deploy failed — post-deploy healthcheck: `crypto unwrap failed (401)`. CI job: `vault-unlock` step exited 1.

lia-security: checklist to confirm:
- confirm app principal (service principal) exists in the vault tenant (guest SP vs local app). cross-tenant apps often require the app to be consented/created in target tenant.
- verify RBAC role assignment on the vault resource (not subscription unless intentional).
- enable Key Vault diagnostic settings -> send `AuditEvent` and `Microsoft.KeyVault` categories to Log Analytics + storage account for long-term audit. saves `UnwrapKey` denies for incident triage.
- for rotation: ensure new key version is published and that Redwood's rewrap job uses `get` + `wrapKey` against new key version, then swap pointers. schedule rewrap with retry window to avoid dropped decrypts.

sam-sre: ops options we've used: 
1) create an app registration in the customer's tenant (preferred for customer-managed vaults). add federated cred there (GH Actions) and role-assign `Key Vault Crypto User`. this avoids cross-tenant SP issues.
2) if you cannot create app in customer tenant, have the customer invite your SP as an enterprise application (guest) and then role-assign it. they need to consent to the app.
3) if using user-assigned MI: it must exist in the same tenant/subscription as the vault — MI cannot span tenants. so user-assigned MI is not a cross-tenant solution.

kevin: also note subtle RBAC vs access-policy gotcha — if the vault is using access policies model (legacy), RBAC role assignments won't grant crypto ops. confirm `properties.enablePurgeProtection` or `properties.enableSoftDelete` settings separately. there is no single click migration; check `az keyvault show --name <vault>` and inspect `properties.enableRbacAuthorization` flag.

arjun: helpful — do you have a short playbook we can hand to the customer's infra team so they can set this up quickly?

marta: yep — pared down playbook to copy/paste for customer: 
1) customer creates an App Registration in their tenant (name: `redwood-<org>-kv-client`) and creates a service principal. note object id.
2) add federated credential in GH Actions for that app (if you want workload identity): map repo -> subject.
3) role assignment: run the `az role assignment create` command above using the app object id, scope = vault resource id. role = `Key Vault Crypto User`.
4) verify key permissions: `az keyvault key show --vault-name <vault> --name <cmk>` then ensure ops include `unwrapKey`/`wrapKey`.
5) enable diagnostic settings: `az monitor diagnostic-settings create --resource <vault-id> --workspace <log-analytics-id> --logs '[[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'` (customer to provide workspace).

sam-sre: test steps: 
- customer grants role, then run `az account get-access-token --resource https://vault.azure.net` using the app creds (or `az rest` with client credentials) and call `https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/keys/<key>/unwrap?api-version=7.3` with test ciphertext. should return 200 if perms are correct.

lia-security: one more security bit — rotate keys regularly and keep previous key versions available for a TTL window during rewrap. enable soft-delete & purge protection on vaults storing CMKs to prevent accidental deletion during rotation.

arjun: awesome, copying this into the customer ticket. i'll try option #1 and ask them to run the playbook. i'll post logs after they do the role assignment. thanks all :thumbsup:
